top.name: Preset menu
top.tip: Preset list: factory presets first, then your own.

top.name: Save
top.tip: Save the current sound. Overwrite your own preset or save as a new one.

top.name: Delete
top.tip: Delete your preset. Factory presets cannot be deleted.

top.name: Export
top.tip: Show the preset as text you can copy.

top.name: Import
top.tip: Paste preset text. It is checked before it is used.

top.name: Audio (mockup page only)
top.tip: Audio on or off. Browsers need one click before they play sound.

top.name: Guide
top.tip: Opens the short guide: how to use Instrument and FX, Freeze, Hold, Capture, Riser and Thicken, the Key to keys, and how to see a hint.

top.name: Settings
top.tip: Menu: info bubbles on or off, power saving, show grains on the display, reset the window size to 100%, open the GitHub page.

top.name: About & Support
top.tip: Studio 87, version, licence (AGPL-3.0-or-later), where your saved sounds live, and the Support on Ko-fi button. Nothing is sent anywhere; the button only opens a link when you click it.

top.name: Window size
top.tip: Window size, percent of the default. Drag any edge or corner to resize; double click the wood to go back to 100%.

items.name: Mode
items.tip: Instrument plays the loaded sample with MIDI. FX works on the audio passing through the track. (Instrument / FX)

items.name: Audio source
items.tip: Instrument: the sound you play with the keys. FX: the audio that passes through the track. In the plugin FX listens to the track; here you pick a loop or drop a file.

items.name: Freeze
items.tip: FX: stop recording and loop what is in the buffer. Grains then play only the frozen audio.

items.name: Hold
items.tip: Holds the playing position still. Click to latch, or press and hold for a stutter.

items.name: Play
items.tip: Instrument: plays the sound at its root key and keeps playing until you press again. You can also click the piano keys. FX: the loop plays by itself.

items.name: Riser
items.tip: Starts the riser: grains shrink, get closer and fuse into a pitched tone while pitch and filter climb.

items.name: Capture
items.tip: FX: record what the buffer holds into Hairball as a small sample and switch to Instrument to play it.

items.name: Capture
items.tip: How many seconds of the incoming audio Hairball keeps ready to freeze (FX mode). (0.50 s to 8.00 s, default 4.00 s)

items.name: Lag
items.tip: FX mode, not frozen: how far behind the live audio the grains read. (0.0 ms to 2.00 s, default 120 ms)

items.name: Dry/wet
items.tip: Blend between the untouched input and Hairball. At 0 the input passes bit for bit. (0% to 100%, default 100%)

items.name: Output
items.tip: Output level. (-24.0 dB to +12.0 dB, default 0.0 dB)

items.name: Limiter
items.tip: Safety limiter at the output, never above 0 dBFS. (Off / On)

items.name: Nasty range
items.tip: Lets Drive, Transistor and Fuzz go beyond 100 percent. Off by default. (Off / On)

items.name: Attack
items.tip: Fade in and fade out of each grain. Added to the grain length on both ends. (0.0 ms to 250 ms, default 20.0 ms)

items.name: Hold len
items.tip: Length each grain plays before the next one takes over. (2.0 ms to 800 ms, default 80.0 ms)

items.name: Gr. spacing
items.tip: Gap between grains. 100 percent places them end to end with a clean crossfade. Lower means more overlap and a thicker sound, higher means gaps. (25% to 400%, default 100%)

items.name: Wave spacing
items.tip: How fast the playing position moves through the sound. 100 is normal, 0 freezes, negative plays the grains backwards in order, 300 is three times faster. (-300% to 300%, default 100%)

items.name: Pan
items.tip: Odd grains go left, even grains go right. 0 is off. (0% to 100%, default 0%)

items.name: Depth
items.tip: Size of the LFO that moves Wave spacing. 0 is off. (0% to 300%, default 0%)

items.name: Speed
items.tip: Speed of the LFO on Wave spacing. (0.1 Hz to 30.0 Hz, default 2.0 Hz)

items.name: Rand
items.tip: Randomises where each grain starts, so the order is shuffled. 0 is off. (0% to 100%, default 0%)

items.name: Transients
items.tip: Grains that cross a hit snap to it and take the Transient length. Off, Regions (slices you provide) or Detect (automatic). (Off / Regions / Detect)

items.name: Trans. len
items.tip: Length of grains that start on a transient. (2.0 ms to 400 ms, default 40.0 ms)

items.name: Loop
items.tip: Loop the sound when the position reaches the end. (Off / On)

items.name: Key to
items.tip: What the MIDI keys do: Pitch, Percent (C5 to C7 pick the start position), Step (C5 and up offset the start by steps), Transient (C5 and up pick a slice). (Pitch / Percent / Step / Transient)

items.name: Start
items.tip: Where in the sound playing starts. (0% to 100%, default 0%)

items.name: Root key
items.tip: The MIDI note that plays the sound at its original pitch. (C1 to C7, default C4)

items.name: Pitch
items.tip: Pitch in semitones. Grains are read faster or slower; the position still moves at Wave spacing. (-48.0 st to +48.0 st, default 0.0 st)

items.name: Fine
items.tip: Fine tune in cents. (-100 ct to +100 ct, default 0 ct)

items.name: Env amt
items.tip: Pitch envelope. Starts this many semitones away from the pitch and glides back to it. (-48.0 st to +48.0 st, default 0.0 st)

items.name: Env time
items.tip: How long the pitch envelope takes to return to the set pitch. (5.0 ms to 8.00 s, default 300 ms)

items.name: Env curve
items.tip: Shape of the pitch envelope. Below 1 snaps back fast, above 1 lingers away from the pitch. (0.20x to 5.00x, default 1.00x)

items.name: Glide
items.tip: Instrument: time to slide between notes. (0.0 ms to 2.00 s, default 0.0 ms)

items.name: Attack
items.tip: Instrument: note fade in. (0.0 ms to 4.00 s, default 5.0 ms)

items.name: Decay
items.tip: Instrument: fall to the sustain level. (0.0 ms to 4.00 s, default 200 ms)

items.name: Sustain
items.tip: Instrument: level while the key is held. (0% to 100%, default 100%)

items.name: Release
items.tip: Instrument: note fade out. (0.0 ms to 8.00 s, default 250 ms)

items.name: Voices
items.tip: Instrument: how many notes can play at once. Fewer voices use less CPU. (1 to 8, default 4)

items.name: Riser
items.tip: Starts the riser. In Instrument mode every note starts it. Turn it off and it eases back. (Off / On)

items.name: Follow key
items.tip: Instrument: the riser tone follows the key you play. (Off / On)

items.name: Time
items.tip: How long the riser takes to reach its end. (0.10 s to 32.00 s, default 4.00 s)

items.name: Curve
items.tip: Below 1 jumps up early, above 1 builds slowly and shoots up at the end. (0.20x to 5.00x, default 1.60x)

items.name: Pitch up
items.tip: How many semitones the riser lifts the pitch. (0.0 st to +60.0 st, default +24.0 st)

items.name: Grains
items.tip: How far the grains shrink and speed up as the riser builds. (0% to 100%, default 70%)

items.name: Tone
items.tip: Grains get so close they turn into a pitched tone at the Tone Hz (or the key you play). 0 stays granular. (0% to 100%, default 60%)

items.name: Tone Hz
items.tip: Pitch the grains settle on at the top of the riser (FX mode). (40.0 Hz to 2.00 kHz, default 440 Hz)

items.name: Filter up
items.tip: Opens the filter by this many octaves while the riser builds. (0.0 oct to 6.0 oct, default 2.0 oct)

items.name: Width
items.tip: Mid/side width. 100 is unchanged, 0 is mono, 200 is double the side signal. (0% to 200%, default 100%)

items.name: Bass mono
items.tip: Keeps everything below this frequency in the middle. 0 is off. (0.0 Hz to 400 Hz, default 0.0 Hz)

items.name: Low
items.tip: Low shelf at 120 Hz. (-18.0 dB to +18.0 dB, default 0.0 dB)

items.name: Mid
items.tip: Bell filter gain. (-18.0 dB to +18.0 dB, default 0.0 dB)

items.name: Mid Hz
items.tip: Bell filter frequency. (100 Hz to 8.00 kHz, default 1.00 kHz)

items.name: Mid Q
items.tip: Bell filter width. Higher is narrower. (0.30 to 8.00, default 1.00)

items.name: High
items.tip: High shelf at 8 kHz. (-18.0 dB to +18.0 dB, default 0.0 dB)

items.name: Filter
items.tip: Off, Low pass, High pass or Band pass. (Off / LP / HP / BP)

items.name: Cutoff
items.tip: Filter cutoff. The riser can open it by itself. (20.0 Hz to 20.00 kHz, default 12.00 kHz)

items.name: Reso
items.tip: Filter resonance. (0.50 to 12.00, default 0.70)

items.name: Drive
items.tip: Symmetric analog clip. Odd harmonics, loud and bright. Above 100 percent needs Nasty range. (0% to 200%, default 0%)

items.name: Transistor
items.tip: Neve style asymmetric stage. Even harmonics, warm and thick. Above 100 percent needs Nasty range. (0% to 200%, default 0%)

items.name: Fuzz
items.tip: Lopsided hard fuzz. Above 80 percent it turns nasty on purpose. Above 100 percent needs Nasty range. (0% to 200%, default 0%)

items.name: Dance
items.tip: Glue compressor on everything above 150 Hz, bass left alone. Pumps and holds the sound together for dance music. (0% to 100%, default 0%)
